subject: Post-demo: tail targets, throughput constraints, and streaming checklist

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-demo: tail targets, throughput constraints, and streaming checklist

Hi Maya —

Great to meet the Brightseed engineering team today. Short recap and the asks we captured on the call so our performance team can scope an apples-to-apples hosted comparison vs your current provider: 

Key targets you called out
- p95 end-to-end (user request -> first token) target: <= 120ms for short prompts (<= 64 tokens)
- p99: <= 320ms for the same envelope
- Sustained throughput target: 1,000 requests/minute per region during peak windows
- Concurrency: typical concurrency per app instance ~35; burst to 120 for 60s windows
- Streaming: server-sent chunk size ~64 tokens, client expects first token within 80ms of request for streaming flows

What we need from Brightseed to finalize the hosted-vs-incumbent comparison
1) Confirmation: your current provider’s measured p95/p99 for the production traffic envelope (numbers or recent runbook results) — ideally a CSV or brief report.
2) Traffic profile: % short (<=64 tokens) vs medium vs long, and distribution over the peak minute.
3) Any request-level preprocessing that you do in front of the model (dedup, signature verification) that adds fixed latency (avg ms).
4) Authentication: are you using mTLS or token-based auth for API calls? Any added handshakes?

I attached the list of SLO asks you shared and a blank latency probe plan we use for hosted comparisons. If you can drop the incumbent numbers and the traffic profile into the attached latency_probe_plan.xlsx, we’ll ship a side-by-side comparison with expected p95/p99 deltas and a recommended traffic-shaping strategy.

Next steps
- Maya: drop incumbent metrics and the traffic profile into the attached sheet (or reply with CSV) — target EOD Friday PT if possible.
- I’ll loop in Ben and Jonas for the hosted probe design once we have the numbers.

Thanks — appreciate the team's time.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Vanessa —

Thanks for the crisp recap and the template. Quick clarifications from our side before we complete the sheet: 
- Our current p95/p99 numbers are measured from edge->app->model (so they include a 12–18ms edge hop plus auth). We can provide both edge-observed and model-only if useful.
- Streaming expectation: client wants first token within 80–100ms for UI snappyness. This is tight for longer context runs; our streaming flows are typically short prompts.
- Auth: token-based bearer auth for most traffic; internal services use mTLS. No extra pre-processing for the real-time path.

We’ll populate the latency_probe_plan.xlsx and upload by EOD Friday (may push to Monday if our infra team needs a quick run). I’m attaching the incumbent run summary we have (incumbent-run-summary.csv) — it’s an export from our monitoring pipeline and includes p95/p99 for the last 10M requests.

Thanks,
Maya

2) Streaming behavior: they expect first-token within ~80–100ms. From an implementation POV we need to pick chunking and keep-alive thresholds. What are reasonable defaults and which flags should we expose to them?

Maya attached an incumbent-run-summary.csv (see thread). I’ve attached our hosted-vs-incumbent-quick-matrix.pdf to this forward to highlight typical delta drivers. 

Appreciate quick turnaround — aiming to have Ben/Jonas recommended probe config and suggested defaults by tomorrow morning so we can reply with a scoped doc and a timeline.

— Vanessa

Quick summary of recommended probe and defaults — high level first, details attached.

Summary recommendations
- Probe approach: shadow traffic run inside their staging region with identical request envelope (token counts and inter-arrival distribution). Run at 1x and 1.5x their stated sustained throughput (1,000 rpm -> run at 1,000 and 1,500 rpm) for 30-minute windows to capture steady-state and burst.
- Instance sizing: use 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (or 6x for quantized model) in the test pool per region. Configure continuous batching with batch timeout 8ms to favor latency for short prompts.
- Concurrency: reserve pool concurrency of 120 and soft limits at 90 to allow bursts; streaming sessions count vs compute should be tracked separately (we recommend limiting streaming sessions per compute to 60 to hit first-token windows).
- Streaming defaults: chunk size 64 tokens, first-chunk flush-after 30ms or after receiving first token; enable prefix KV cache for repeated prompts. This gets first-token often < 80ms for short prompts under the sizing above.
- Observability: collect per-request trace with timestamps at client-recv, edge-arrive, auth-complete, model-infer-start, first-token, last-token.

Attachments included: latency_probe_plan_filled.xlsx (we pre-filled with expected deltas), hosted-vs-incumbent-quick-matrix.pdf (drivers and expected impact), probe-run-ops-checklist.txt (runbook).

I’ll sync with Jonas offline to validate the GPU mix and batching knobs; happy to jump on a quick call with Brightseed to walk the probe plan.
